'''Lewis Richard Benjamin Elton''' (born '''Ludwig Richard Benjamin Ehrenberg'''; 25 March 1923 – 29 September 2018) was a German-born British physicist and researcher into education, specialising in higher education.

==Early life==
Born in [[Tübingen]] to the scholars [[Victor Ehrenberg (historian)|Victor Ehrenberg]] and Eva Dorothea Sommer, Ehrenberg moved with his family to [[Prague]] in 1929, and from there to England in February 1939, to escape [[History of the Jews in Germany#Jews under the Nazis (1933–45)|Nazi persecution of the Jews]]. Ehrenberg naturalised as a British subject and changed his name by deed poll in June 1947.<ref>{{London Gazette |issue=38000 |date=27 June 1947 |page=29972}}</ref><ref>{{London Gazette |issue=38019 |date=18 July 1947 |page=3342}}</ref> He was educated at [[Rydal Penrhos|Rydal School]] in [[Colwyn Bay]], and thereafter at [[Christ's College, Cambridge]], the [[University of Westminster|Regent Street Polytechnic]], London, and [[University College London]]. It was from the latter institution that he was awarded his PhD, in 1950.{{cn|date=September 2026}}

==Career==
He was Professor of Physics at Battersea College of Technology from 1964 until 1970. The College completed its transformation into the [[University of Surrey]] (and its relocation from [[Battersea]] to [[Guildford]]) in 1970. He founded the Institute of Educational Technology<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.surrey.ac.uk/news/ben-elton-remembers-his-father|title=Ben Elton remembers his father {{!}} University of Surrey|website=www.surrey.ac.uk|access-date=2020-04-21}}</ref>  in 1967, the first of its kind. He was somewhat of a pioneer and innovator in the professional development of university teachers and became Professor of Higher Education in 1970, a post he held until 1988.{{cn|date=September 2026}} The Institute became internationally renowned and his philosophy is one that has been adopted by many universities around the world.{{cn|date=September 2026}}

In 1994, he was appointed Professor of Higher Education at [[University College London]], where he founded the Higher Education Research and Development Unit (now the Centre for the Advancement of Learning and Teaching). He became an honorary professor there in 2003. He was appointed Visiting Professor of Higher Education at [[Manchester University]] in August 2005.{{cn|date=September 2026}}

He was a Fellow of the [[American Institute of Physics]] and a Fellow of the [[Society for Research into Higher Education]]. He was awarded a Lifetime Achievement award at the 2005 Times Higher Awards,<ref>{{Citation | last = Thomson | first = Alan | title = Proud winners and PM sparkle at first awards | newspaper = Times Higher Education | location = London | date   = 2 December 2005 | url    = http://www.timeshighereducation.co.uk/news/proud-winners-and-pm-sparkle-at-first-awards/200100.article |accessdate=29 June 2013 }}</ref> at which [[Helena Kennedy|Baroness Kennedy]] said "there is a polymath quality to this man that points to someone interested in educating the whole person."<ref>{{Citation |date = December 2005 |title = Manchester wins 'higher education institution of the year' award | journal = UniLife |publisher = The University of Manchester | location = Manchester | volume = 3 | issue = 3 | pages  = 3 | url=http://documents.manchester.ac.uk/display.aspx?DocID=7361 | accessdate=29 June 2013 }}</ref>

==Lewis Elton Gallery, University of Surrey==
In 1963, at the Surrey University Battersea campus, Elton started a project to show original artworks in the Physics Department.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.surrey.ac.uk/arts/visualarts/exhibitions%20and%20events/the_elton_art_collection_exhibition.htm |title=the lewis and mary elton art collection - University of Surrey - Guildford |website=www.surrey.ac.uk |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120513154034/http://surrey.ac.uk/arts/visualarts/exhibitions%20and%20events/the_elton_art_collection_exhibition.htm |archive-date=2012-05-13}}</ref> When the University Gallery at Guildford was relocated in 1997, the gallery was dedicated to Elton and was named the [[Lewis Elton Gallery]]. The gallery hosts regular exhibitions of paintings, photographs and sculpture.

==Lewis and Mary Elton Art Collection==
The donation of a collection of paintings and [[objets d'art]] was made to [[University of Surrey]] including works by [[Picasso]], [[Chagall]], [[Klee]] and [[Cocteau]]. The gift was marked by an exhibition at [[The Lightbox]] gallery, Woking, in January 2012.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.surrey.ac.uk/arts/visualarts/exhibitions%20and%20events/the_elton_art_collection_exhibition.htm |title=the lewis and mary elton art collection - University of Surrey - Guildford |website=www.surrey.ac.uk |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120513154034/http://surrey.ac.uk/arts/visualarts/exhibitions%20and%20events/the_elton_art_collection_exhibition.htm |archive-date=2012-05-13}}</ref>

==Personal life and death==
His older brother was the historian [[Geoffrey Elton]]. Lewis married Mary Foster,<ref>{{Cite web |author=Guardian Staff |date=2000-05-24 |title=Ben Elton: from Peter Pan to Maybe Baby |url=http://www.theguardian.com/film/2000/may/24/1 |access-date=2022-10-21 |website=the Guardian |language=en}}</ref> whom he met at university and one of their four<ref>{{Cite web |last=Ashe |first=Eliza |date=2012-12-01 |title=What I know about women |url=https://www.smh.com.au/lifestyle/what-i-know-about-women-20121127-2a5e2.html |access-date=2022-10-22 |website=The Sydney Morning Herald |language=en}}</ref> children is the comedian and author [[Ben Elton]]. Lewis died in September 2018, aged 95.<ref name=":0">[https://www.surrey.ac.uk/news/professor-lewis-elton-remembered Professor Lewis Elton remembered]</ref>
